### D555 — refine reads a device's SVD with its own strict XML reader

**The tour said** nothing of how a chip is learnt. D542 makes a device a
description in Landin source whose interrupts are generated from the
device's CMSIS-SVD file, and the register modules were generated by a
Python script that only the repository could run, while no feature of the
compiler may need Python and no new runtime dependency is admitted
without the maintainer.

**Chosen:** `refine` reads the SVD itself, through `Landin.Xml`, a reader of
XML 1.0's well-formed documents in the subset an SVD is written in: an
optional byte order mark and XML declaration whose encoding is UTF-8,
elements, attributes, character data with the five predefined entities and
character references decoded and line ends read as XML says, CDATA
sections, comments and processing instructions. It refuses, never raises,
and places each refusal by line and byte column: a document type
declaration and every entity but the five, bytes that are not UTF-8 and
characters XML does not admit, an end tag that closes something else, an
attribute given twice, `<` in an attribute value, `]]>` in character data,
`--` in a comment, text outside the root element, and nesting deeper than 64
elements. A refused SVD is L0525.

**The alternatives:** an XML library, a dependency the maintainer has not
agreed and one that reads more than an SVD is written in; a forgiving
reader, which would generate modules from a file nobody can say was read as
written; and keeping the generator in Python, which makes learning a chip
the repository's privilege rather than the compiler's.

**Pinned by** the `xml` suite: `elements are read`, `references are
decoded`, `every refusal is placed`, which names each refusal with its line
and column, and `hostile bytes never raise`.

### D556 — `refine svd` reads an SVD and a selection policy

**The tour said** nothing. An SVD describes every register of a chip, most
of them with less care than a generated access deserves, so what is
generated is a reviewed selection, and the review belongs to one exact
file.

**Chosen:** `refine svd --policy=POLICY.json --out-dir=DIR DEVICE.svd`. The
command is named for the format it reads, as `fmt` and `lsp` are for what
they serve. The policy is JSON, read by the reader refine already has for
its language server, and it has schema 2. It names the SVD it was reviewed
against by `device`, `svd_version` and `svd_sha256`, and an SVD that is not
that file is L0527: a review covers one file, not its successors. It gives
the `notice` lines each module begins with, which is where a derivative
carries the licensor's notice; the layout under the output directory, as
`modules`, `prefix`, `correspondence`, `manifest` and `description`, each
with a default; the `selection`, each peripheral's registers in the order
they are generated; one access policy per selected register, its `read`
`normal`, `modify` or `refused`, its `write` `normal`, `one_clears` or
`refused`, its `reserved` bits `zero` or `preserve` and an optional
`write_mask`; `numeric_enums`, the fields whose vendor enumeration is read
as a number; `reset_mask_overrides`, the reset knowledge a reviewer
promises instead of the SVD's; and `reset_corrections`, a reviewed reset
value with the source it was read from; and `field_corrections`, a field's
reviewed `bits` or that it is to be omitted, or a field the SVD lacks,
added with its `bits` and `access` (D652), with its `source`, which the
correspondence records beside the SVD's; and `interrupt_corrections`, an
interrupt to add or move to a `value`, or to `omit`, with its `source`,
which `interrupts.ldn` says in a line of its own (D542). Any other member is refused, except
`provenance`, the reviewer's notes, which is not read. A policy refine
cannot read is L0526, and one that selects what the SVD lacks L0530.

**The alternatives:** a policy written in Landin source as tool directives,
which would make a review note a program the compiler checks and the
editor tooling reaches, but which no program imports and whose directives
would be a second language beside D542's; a policy in the SVD's own XML,
which a reviewer edits in the vendor's file; and command-line selection,
which leaves no reviewed record of what was chosen.

**Pinned by** `devices/policies/rp2040.json` and
`devices/policies/stm32h753.json`, the `devices` suite's `every refusal is
named` and `a correction is recorded`, and `devices/test.py`, which
regenerates both devices from their policies.

### D557 — What the projection reads, and what it writes

**The tour said** at [0740] how a register image is declared and D227 and
D228 how a register is read and written; nothing said how a vendor's
description becomes either.

**Chosen:** each selected register's properties are inherited from the
register, its peripheral, the peripheral that one is derived from, and the
device, in that order; size, reset value, reset mask and access are read so.
A peripheral `derivedFrom` another takes its registers and keeps its own
name and base address, once: a derived peripheral that gives registers of
its own, or is derived from a derived one, is refused. An
`alternateRegister` is a register of its own at the address it shares,
which must be its alternate's, and the correspondence records it. A field
lies where its `bitRange`, its `bitOffset` and `bitWidth`, or its `lsb` and
`msb` say. A register may leave its access to its fields, which must then
each say theirs. A field with enumerated values becomes an encoded type
unless the policy reads it as a number; one without becomes `uN`. Numbers
are decimal, `0x` hexadecimal or `#` binary. Names are lowercased; fields
take `f_`, atoms the register's and field's names, and two vendor names that
become one Landin name are refused. Only 32-bit registers are generated.

L0528 refuses, for a selected register, what is not read: `dim` arrays of
peripherals, registers or fields, a register in a `cluster`, a register or
field derived from another, derived enumerated values, an `alternateGroup`,
a default enumerated value, a number with a multiplier or don't-care bits,
another width, and a core other than the six D542 names. An enumerated
value named otherwise than an identifier cannot be an atom: every selected
field with one is named in one refusal, each with its first such name, and
with the policy's `numeric_enums` as the way out, rather than one field a
run. L0529 refuses
what cannot be generated as it is said: overlapping fields, a field outside
its register, an enumerated value that does not fit or is given twice, a
property given nowhere it is inherited from, an address that is not a
word-aligned 32-bit address, and an alternate at another address.

What is written is the text the RP2040 fixture was first generated in,
byte for byte: one module per selected peripheral, `PREFIX/NAME/device.ldn`;
the correspondence, every selected register and field as the SVD gave it
beside what was generated, as JSON indented by two spaces with sorted keys;
the manifest, each of those files' SHA-256; and `interrupts.ldn` in D542's
text. An SVD without `deviceNumInterrupts` has as many slots as its highest
interrupt needs.

**The alternatives:** expanding arrays and clusters now, which neither
selected device needs and which would be generated untested; merging a
derived peripheral's registers with its parent's, a form neither SVD uses;
and a new text for the modules, which would have cost the byte-for-byte
comparison with what was reviewed.

**Pinned by** the `devices` suite's `a device becomes modules`, which holds
each form's text, and `every refusal is named`; `devices/test.py`'s
regeneration of the RP2040 fixture and the STM32H753 byte for byte and its
mutated-SVD refusal controls.

### D558 — `refine svd` replaces its outputs whole or not at all

**The tour said** nothing. A generator that dies halfway through leaves a
module set that matches no SVD, and its next reader cannot tell.

**Chosen:** D907's shared publication group replaces these outputs. Nothing
is published until every destination is checked: the
output directory must be one, no destination may be a directory or have a
file where a directory is needed, no staged or kept copy of an earlier run
may be beside one, and the manifest found there may name only paths below
it. Each new file is written in exclusive private staging beside its
destination and read back, and only then is each destination replaced,
its old bytes kept until every replacement is done. A failure restores
what this invocation replaced without clobbering a concurrent change, or names the kept
copy it could not put back. A file whose bytes are already the new ones is
left alone. The manifest is how refine knows which files are its own: a file
the old manifest names that this run does not make is removed with the
rest. A refusal before writing is L0531; a write that fails is L0005.
This recovers from a failure; it is not a snapshot for a concurrent reader.

**The alternatives:** writing in place, which the interrupted run defeats;
replacing a whole directory by a rename, which would take the developer's
own files beside the generated ones, and `memory.ldn` is one; and leaving a
deselected module behind, which a program could still import.

**Pinned by** the `devices` suite's `outputs are replaced whole` and
`devices/test.py`'s `a changed output is put back and a stale one removed`.

### D559 — Vendor inputs are pinned by URL and SHA-256 and fetched

**The tour said** nothing. The RP2040's SVD and pico-sdk's headers were
vendored beside the generated modules.

**Chosen:** no vendor input is in the tree. `devices/inputs.json` pins each
SVD and each vendor header the generated modules are checked against by the
URL it is fetched from and its SHA-256, and `scripts/fetch_inputs.py`,
standard-library Python, fetches each into `$LANDIN_INPUTS` or
`~/.cache/landin/inputs`, verifies it every time it is used, and never
caches bytes of another hash. An input its publisher will not serve to
a script, ST's RM0433, is pinned the same way and marked `"fetch": "by
hand"`: a person downloads it and puts it in the cache, and the fetcher
verifies that copy, never downloads one, and without one says where to put
it. No test reads a manual; the literals reviewed from one stay in the
tests, each citing its section and page, and its pinned hash names the
document they were reviewed against. A licence's notice stays in the tree, as a
notice: the generated modules are derivatives of the SVD, BSD-3-Clause asks
that a redistribution of source in any form keep the licence's whole text,
and Apache-2.0 that a recipient be given a copy, so
`devices/notices/LICENSE.pico-sdk` and
`devices/notices/LICENSE-Apache-2.0.stm32h7` are kept and each module's
notice names its own. `check.py` runs `devices/test.py` offline: the lock and
the policies agree, every generated file is the one its manifest hashes and
carries its notice. The regeneration and the vendor-header checks need the
inputs, so the gate's `cortex-m` job fetches them and runs them.

**The alternatives:** a licence line in every module and no licence text,
which keeps neither licence's condition; vendoring the inputs, which the
maintainer declined; and fetching inside `check.py`, which runs offline.

**Pinned by** `scripts/tests/test_fetch_inputs.py`, `devices/test.py`'s
offline tests, and the gate's `cortex-m` steps that fetch and regenerate.

### D820 — `refine bindings` is the binding generator

**The tour said** at [1580] that a separate, deterministic generator reads
headers and writes the declarations. It was a Python script in
`bindings/`, so binding a header needed Python, which no feature of the
compiler may.

**Chosen:** the generator is a command of refine's own, as the SVD importer
is (D555):

`refine bindings --clang=CLANG [--target=NAME] [--sysroot=DIR]
--policy=POLICY.json --out-dir=DIR [--include-dir=DIR]...
[--system-include-dir=DIR]... [--define=NAME[=VALUE]]...
[LOGICAL=]HEADER.h ...`

It is named for what it makes, as `svd` is for what it reads, because what
it reads is C, which names nothing a command could be called. The headers are
its operands, each `LOGICAL=PATH`, or `PATH` named by its last component.
`--target` is refine's own target name, defaulting to the host's as for
every command, and selects its rows: `linux-x86-64`, `linux-arm64` and
`darwin-arm64` have one each, and `cortex-m0` two, AAPCS32's base procedure
call standard and its VFP variant (D935); the policy's `abi.target` must
name one of the target's Clang triples. `--clang` names the Clang by path
or by a name found on PATH, and is required, as the policy, the output
directory and a hosted target's sysroot are (D937): the generator's
contract is that nothing it reads is chosen for it. Paths are
made absolute against the working directory without resolving links.

Within each generated Landin signature, parameter and result names avoid
every identifier used by its types and every other binding in the signature.
Available normalized parameter names are retained; conflicts gain trailing
underscores, with existing suffix names reserved first. Result origin clauses
and parameter metadata use the allocated Landin names; policy names and
`c_name` remain the header's. This applies to direct declarations, adapters,
callback types and incoming handlers. The complete policy reference is a
generated reading page, `bindings.html`, named by installed command help.

Apart from these signature collision repairs, the four outputs retain what
the Python generator wrote: for
every header and policy `bindings/test.py` binds, and for the committed
fixture's on each of the three targets, the same declarations in the same
order, the same adapters and the same metadata with sorted keys, and the
same refusals; each output now says only that `refine bindings` made it.
The policy is unchanged. Clang is asked what it was asked before, in the
same order and with the same arguments, the empty file of D821 aside, and
generation lives in `Landin.Bindings`, a function of what Clang printed, so
the whole generator runs against a fake Clang. What it reads it reads with
`Landin.Json`, and a reserved word is one of `Landin.Tokens`', which
`check.py` holds to the keyword production. Outputs are replaced as D558
replaces refine svd's, every new file written and read back before any is
replaced and a failure putting back what was replaced, rather than by the
Python generator's backup directory. A refusal is a diagnostic: a request
written wrong is L0002, a header or policy that cannot be read L0003, a
policy that is not one L0579, a Clang that cannot be used as asked L0580, a
selection that cannot be bound L0581, outputs in the way L0582, and a
replacement that fails L0005.

**The alternatives:** keeping the Python generator, which the row asked
to retire; Python's own option spellings, `--header` and a Clang triple
for `--target`, which would be the only command whose target is not one of
refine's names; a header parser of refine's own, which [1975] refuses; and
naming the command for its input, `refine c` or `refine header`, which says
less than what it makes. All were declined.

**Pinned by** the `bindings` suite's `a header is bound through a fake
clang`, `requests are refused by code`, `another triple is refused first`,
`plain char must be the row's`, `each target is one row` and `a failed
replacement puts back`; `bindings/test.py`, every case against the pinned
Clang, with `abi/r440-bindings-generated` regenerated byte for byte; and the
gate's `bindings` job. Signature collision consumers are pinned by
`bindings/test.py`'s `test_signature_names_avoid_parameters_and_referenced_types`,
`test_incoming_handler_prototype_avoids_typedef_shadowing` and, on the
adapter-backed Cortex-M paths, `test_cortex_adapter_names_stay_consistent`.

### D821 — Clang runs in an environment of its own, through `Landin.Platform`

**The tour said** nothing. The Python generator ran Clang with an
environment of PATH, HOME and the temporary directory alone, so that no
CPATH, C_INCLUDE_PATH or driver override a shell set could change what a
header means, and refine's tool runner gave every tool the caller's
environment.

**Chosen:** `Landin.Platform`'s tool runner has `Run_In_Environment`, which
runs a program with exactly the environment it is given: an item
`NAME=VALUE` sets a variable, and an item `NAME` passes the caller's own
value on, or nothing when the caller has none. `refine bindings` gives every
Clang run `PATH`, `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `TMP`, `TEMP` and `SystemRoot` as the
caller has them, `LC_ALL=C` and `TZ=UTC`, and nothing else, with
`--no-default-config` and `-nostdinc` as before. Its work, the copied
headers, the preprocessed translation unit and the enum probe, is in a
private directory refine makes and removes. The target's macros are probed
from an empty file in that directory rather than from standard input.
`Landin.Platform`'s filesystem also says whether a path is a symbolic link,
so the output directory, and each output, is refused when one is.

**The alternatives:** inheriting the caller's environment, which would let
CPATH supply a header the request never named; clearing it entirely, which
leaves Clang no PATH to find its own tools by; and wrapping Clang in `env`,
a second program between refine and the one it means to run.

**Pinned by** the `bindings` suite's `a header is bound through a fake
clang`, which holds every Clang call to that environment, and
`bindings/test.py`'s `ambient include variables are excluded from every
clang invocation`.

### D935 — `refine bindings` binds C for Cortex-M under AAPCS32, in both procedure call standards

**The tour said** at [1580] that the generator writes the declarations a
header's C needs, and nothing about a target without LP64. The generator
knew three LP64 rows, and its macro check, its builtin sizes and its
metadata were LP64's.

**Chosen:** `--target=cortex-m0`, refine's one M-profile target name, has
two rows, because a description's float unit changes the C convention while
the target name stays (D615): AAPCS32's base procedure call standard, Clang
triple `thumbv6m-unknown-none-eabi` with `-mfloat-abi=soft`, and its VFP
variant, `thumbv7em-unknown-none-eabihf` with `-mfpu=fpv5-d16
-mfloat-abi=hard`, the one float unit D615 admits. The triples are the
spellings Clang prints for `-print-target-triple`, which the generator
compares with the row's. The policy chooses the row: `abi.target` names its
triple, and `abi.calling_convention`, `aapcs` or `aapcs-vfp`, the name
`bindings.json` records as `calling_convention`, is required for
`cortex-m0` and must be the triple's, so the VFP variant is never chosen by
a triple's `hf` alone; on the other targets the key may be given and must be
the row's. `abi.data_model` is `ilp32` for both rows and for no other, and
`plain_char` is `unsigned`. Both rows assert `compiler.c_aapcs32` and are
freestanding (D937, D938). Clang's answer for an empty file is held to
`__ILP32__`, a four-byte `long`, pointer, `size_t` and `ptrdiff_t`,
`__arm__`, `__thumb__`, `__ARM_EABI__`, `__ARM_ARCH_PROFILE` `'M'`,
`__ELF__`, `__ARM_PCS`, `__ARM_SIZEOF_MINIMAL_ENUM` 4 under the
`-fno-short-enums` every run gets, `__STDC_HOSTED__` 0, an unsigned plain
`char` and little-endian storage, and `__ARM_PCS_VFP` is required exactly
for the VFP row, with `__ARM_FP` `0xe` there and no `__ARM_FP` for the base
one. A `long` and a pointer are the row's word in every layout the
generator computes, so a native record's generated offset assertions are
ILP32's. `long double`, a double under AAPCS32, stays refused as on every
target. `NVIC_EnableIRQ` and its kin are CMSIS macros naming
`__NVIC_EnableIRQ`; the generator binds no macro, so a policy selects the
function and gives it a Landin name.

**The alternatives:** a refine target per convention, which refine does not
have: the float unit is the description's and a level is not a target;
`--float-abi` on the command line, which would make the command line rather
than the reviewed policy say which ABI a binding is for; choosing the row by
the triple alone, whose suffix is the whole difference; and Clang's shorter
spellings `thumbv6m-none-eabi` and `thumbv7em-none-eabihf`, which it
accepts and prints otherwise, so the triple check would compare two
spellings of one target. All were declined.

**Pinned by** the `bindings` suite's `each target is one row`, `cortex-m
macros are aapcs32's`, `ilp32 is the aapcs32 policy's` and `a cortex-m
header is bound freestanding`, and `bindings/test.py`'s
`test_cortex_targets_bind_ilp32_in_both_conventions`,
`test_cortex_rejects_an_lp64_or_other_convention_clang` and
`test_cortex_policy_is_ilp32_and_names_its_convention`.

### D936 — A Cortex-M binding asserts its float unit beside `compiler.c_aapcs32`

**The tour said** nothing. One fact, `compiler.c_aapcs32`, holds under both
procedure call standards, so a binding asserting it alone would let a
program built for a description with a float unit import bindings whose
adapters take floats in core registers, while the program passes them in
the float unit's.

**Chosen:** a base binding asserts `compiler.assert(not
compiler.feature.fp)` and a VFP one `compiler.assert(compiler.feature.fp_dp)`
on the line after its ABI fact, so the program built for the other
convention is refused when it is compiled. The VFP assertion is `fp_dp`
rather than `fp` because its adapters were compiled for FPv5-D16 and may
use its double-precision instructions.

**The alternatives:** a second fact per convention, which the compiler does
not have and which `compiler.feature` already decides; and leaving the
mismatch to the linker's `Tag_ABI_VFP_args` attributes, which refuse only at
link time and only where a link checks them. Both were declined.

**Pinned by** the `bindings` suite's `a cortex-m header is bound
freestanding`, and `bindings/test.py`'s
`test_cortex_targets_bind_ilp32_in_both_conventions` and
`test_cortex_bindings_refuse_a_program_of_the_other_convention`, which
compiles both committed bindings for `cortex-m0` without a float unit and
with the AN500 lane's FPv5-D16 description, and each is refused with L0324
by the other.

### D937 — A freestanding target's C headers are Clang's own, as the request names them

**The tour said** nothing. The generator passed `-nostdinc` and a required
`--sysroot`, and a binding that needed `<stdarg.h>` named Clang's resource
directory with `--system-include-dir`.

**Chosen:** `cortex-m0` is freestanding. It has no system root: `--sysroot`
is refused for it, and stays required for the hosted rows, which refine now
says once it knows the target. Clang gets `-ffreestanding`, so
`__STDC_HOSTED__` is 0 and Clang's `<stdint.h>` uses no library's, and still
`-nostdinc`, so its freestanding headers, `<stdint.h>`, `<stddef.h>`,
`<stdbool.h>` and `<stdarg.h>` among them, are reached only through the
`--system-include-dir` naming `$(clang -print-resource-dir)/include`, a root
like any other the request names. A host C library's header is not found.

**The alternatives:** `-nostdlibinc`, which keeps Clang's resource directory
implicitly, an unnamed root that the marker check and the file-prefix maps
would have to learn and that D820's contract, nothing it reads chosen for
it, excludes; and requiring an empty `--sysroot` as for a hosted target,
which names a directory a freestanding target does not have. Both were
declined.

**Pinned by** the `bindings` suite's `a cortex-m header is bound
freestanding` and `requests are refused by code`, and `bindings/test.py`'s
`test_cortex_headers_are_clangs_freestanding_ones_alone`.

### D938 — Freestanding adapters allocate nothing and reach no C library

**The tour said** nothing. Generated adapters allocated C-owned objects and
nullable-callback cells with `calloc` and `free`, and reached a
`_Thread_local` object through the C library's thread pointer.

**Chosen:** on `cortex-m0` a C-owned union, bitfield or opaque record gets
its copy, size, alignment and member accessors and no `allocate` or
`release`: its caller supplies the storage by its size and alignment, from
an arena or a fixed buffer, and the metadata's `lifecycle` records the two
as null. `adapters.c` then includes no `<stdlib.h>`. A nullable callback,
whose cell's `allocate` and `release` are `calloc` and `free`, is refused
with L0581, which says to select it with `nullable: false` and give its
positions nonnullable policy; a non-null callback is an ordinary `extern(c)`
callable. A `_Thread_local` object, which Arm code reaches through
`__aeabi_read_tp`, is refused with L0581 too. By-value wrappers, wrappers of
internal inline definitions, object accessors and incoming-varargs entries,
whose `<stdarg.h>` is freestanding, are generated as on a hosted target.
`adapters.c` is compiled for the row's triple before publication, as on
every target.

**The alternatives:** a C allocator the generated C would call, which a
freestanding image does not have; and nullable-callback cells without
`allocate` and `release`, as an object has, which `initialize` already
allows for caller storage. That one is declined until a firmware consumer
passes a nullable callback; until then the refusal says what to do instead.

**Pinned by** `bindings/test.py`'s `test_cortex_adapters_are_freestanding`.

### D939 — Cortex-M bindings are checked against pinned CMSIS headers

**The tour said** nothing. The pinned device inputs were SVDs and register
headers (D559); no CMSIS-Core header was pinned.

**Chosen:** `devices/inputs.json` pins, by URL and SHA-256, the CMSIS
headers two Cortex-M bindings read. From pico-sdk's commit `a1438dff`, the
SVD's: the CMSIS stub's `RP2040.h`, `system_RP2040.h`, `core_cm0plus.h`,
`cmsis_version.h`, `cmsis_compiler.h`, `cmsis_clang.h`, `cmsis_gcc.h` and
`m-profile/cmsis_clang_m.h`, `m-profile/cmsis_gcc_m.h` and
`m-profile/armv7m_mpu.h`, the compiler headers of both Clang and GCC, as
`rp2040-cmsis/`. For the pinned `stm32h753xx.h`, the CMSIS-Core 5.9 it
includes, `core_cm7.h`, `cmsis_version.h`, `cmsis_compiler.h`,
`cmsis_gcc.h`, `mpu_armv7.h` and `cachel1_armv7.h`, from STM32CubeH7's
commit `8ec3113d`, whose device submodule is the pinned cmsis-device-h7
`81db1ec6`, and that commit's `system_stm32h7xx.h`, as `stm32h753-cmsis/`.
Arm's CMSIS licence text is `devices/notices/LICENSE-Apache-2.0.cmsis`. Two
ABI fixtures hold the four outputs: `abi/cortex-cmsis-bindings`, for the base
standard, selects `IRQn_Type` and the static inline `__NVIC_EnableIRQ`,
`__NVIC_GetEnableIRQ`, `__NVIC_DisableIRQ`, `__NVIC_GetPendingIRQ`,
`__NVIC_SetPendingIRQ`, `__NVIC_ClearPendingIRQ`, `__NVIC_SetPriority`,
`__NVIC_GetPriority` and `SysTick_Config` from `RP2040.h`; and
`abi/cortex-vfp-bindings`, for the VFP variant, selects the STM32H753's
`IRQn_Type`, five NVIC functions and `SCB_GetFPUType`, and, since neither
CMSIS core has an inline function taking a float or a double, the float and
double interface of the fixture's own `landin-vfp.h`. The register structs
the headers declare `volatile` are not selected and refuse nothing. Their
adapters are compiled with `-fno-short-enums`, which the pinned
`arm-eabi-gcc`, whose default enums are short, needs as Clang's
`-fno-short-enums` does; the generated compatible-type assertions refuse
the build without it.

**The alternatives:** vendoring the headers, declined as D559 declines it;
Arm's CMSIS_5 tag 5.9.0 for `core_cm7.h`, rather than the copy ST releases
its device header against; and the STM32H753's own headers for the VFP
interface, which have none. All were declined.

**Pinned by** `bindings/test.py`'s
`test_cortex_fixtures_are_exactly_regenerable`, which fetches the inputs,
regenerates both fixtures byte for byte and compiles their C for each row,
and `test_cortex_adapters_build_with_the_pinned_arm_gcc`.

### D585 — The gate builds the flake on every run that does not reuse a pass

**The tour said** nothing. `nix build .#refine`, the documented default,
failed unnoticed from 2026-10-08, "build/nix/release/generated is not a valid
directory", because nothing in CI built the flake: it was built by hand,
and Nix CI was deferred.

**Chosen:** the gate has a `flake` job. It runs `nix build .#refine
.#refine-bin`, `nix flake check --no-build --all-systems`, which evaluates
every package and the development shell of every system, and
`nix develop --command ./scripts/toolchain.sh` on Linux x86-64. It runs on
every gate run that does not reuse a pass, manual dispatch included, so a
change anywhere in the source that breaks `nix build .#refine`, as the
failure above was, fails the commit that makes it. Under a reused pass it
is skipped with the other lanes, and the reuse list requires it, so the
run reused built the flake from the same tree, or from one that differs
only in the four documents no lane reads. That is the whole of Nix CI: no
derivation is cached, and the only other job that uses nix, `rv64-qemu`,
takes its emulator from the flake.

**The alternatives:** building only when `flake.nix`, `flake.lock` or
`environments/pins.sh` changed, decided by a diff against the event's base
or by GitHub's record of the last build from the same three files: either
leaves a source change that breaks the source build unseen until those
files next change or the record expires, and a diff also skips wrongly
after a run whose flake build failed. The maintainer chose to build on every
run. And the whole of Nix CI, cached derivations and the test suite under
nix, which the maintainer limited to building the flake.

**Pinned by** the gate's `flake` job, and `scripts/tests/test_gate_inputs.py`'s
`Workflow` case, which holds the reuse list to every job the aggregate
needs, `flake` among them.

### D586 — An explanatory edit may take its base from any branch's full run

**The tour said** nothing. The explanatory exception took its base only
from a full run of a push to main, so a documents-only commit that closed
an item after its branch's full gate cost one more full run before main
could reuse it.

**Chosen:** under the explanatory exception the base is any complete
successful push run of this repository from the preceding seven days, of
main or of another branch, and a push to any branch of this repository may
itself use the exception, as a push to main and a same-repository pull
request by an author with write access could. Everything else stands: the
tree differs from the base only in the content of the four top-level
documents no lane reads, which `scripts/gate_inputs.py` lists; the base is
an ancestor of every tip; every commit since it says `Gate: explanatory`; every required
job, every matrix leg by its name, succeeded in a complete listing; and a
run that itself reused a pass never supplies one. A branch's run is as
trustworthy a base as main's because only someone with write access can
push to a branch, and the tree key covers the workflow that run executed
and every tool pin: a run of a weakened workflow can be reused only by a
tree that still carries it, as with identical-tree reuse.

**The alternatives:** closing every item before its gate, which the
process asked and which a finding after the gate defeats; and keeping main
as the only base, which spends a full run on prose.

**Pinned by** `scripts/tests/test_gate_inputs.py`'s
`test_a_full_run_of_another_branch_is_a_record` and
`test_a_branch_push_may_use_the_exception`, and the `Decide` cases that
hold ancestry, declarations and the complete listing.

### D560 — The STM32H753 is learnt for prototype 1's UART and DMA, with reviewed corrections

**The tour said** nothing of a second family. Prototype 1 drives a UART
through DMA beside a timer; the maintainer's rig has a NUCLEO-H753ZI, whose
ST-LINK virtual COM port is USART3 on PD8 and PD9.

**Chosen:** the STM32H753 is learnt from ST's own SVD, the copy in Arm's
`STM32H7xx_DFP` at tag `v4.1.3`, under Apache-2.0, pinned by hash and not
vendored. Its policy selects the RCC clock enables for GPIO port D, USART3
and DMA1 (`AHB4ENR`, `APB1LENR`, `AHB1ENR`); port D's `MODER` and `AFRH`, for
PD8 and PD9's alternate function 7; USART3's `CR1`, `CR3`, `BRR`, `ISR`,
`ICR`, `RDR` and `TDR`; DMA1's `LISR`, `LIFCR` and stream 0's `S0CR`,
`S0NDTR`, `S0PAR` and `S0M0AR`; DMAMUX1's channel 0, `DMAMUX_C0CR`; and
TIM2's `CCMR1_Input`, prototype 1's timer and the selection's alternate
register. These use every form D557 reads: GPIOD and USART3 are derived
from GPIOA and USART1, every reset mask is the device's, and no selected
field but DMAMUX1's enumerates values, which are read as numbers. Status is
read and not written, a clear register written as one-clears and not read,
and USART3's receive register read with one load.

Where the SVD and ST's CMSIS header disagree, the reference manual decides:
RM0433 Rev 9, pinned by its SHA-256 and supplied by hand (D559). Where it
says the SVD is wrong, the policy carries a reviewed correction with the
section and page it was read at: `RCC_AHB1ENR`'s bit 18 is reserved, not a
field (8.7.41, p. 454); port D's mode register resets to 0xFFFF FFFF, all
analog, where the SVD gives port A's 0xABFF FFFF by deriving port D from it
(11.4.1, p. 541); and the RAMECC diagnostic interrupt is at 145, which the
SVD omits (Table 147, p. 759). It is named `ECC`, the header's `ECC_IRQn`,
because the manual gives that one line three acronyms, `RAMECC1` to
`RAMECC3`. Where it says the SVD is right, nothing is corrected and the
check names the header's disagreement: DMAMUX1's `DMAREQ_ID` is bits 6:0
and `SYNC_ID` bits 26:24 (17.6.1, p. 708), where the header's masks are
DMAMUX2's, and `WWDG1_RST` is at 143, which the header omits.

A policy may so add, move or remove an interrupt, each with a cited
source, as it corrects a field. `interrupts.ldn` then carries the corrected
table, and D542's form says each correction in a line of its own after the
line that says the file is generated from the SVD, so a reader of the
description sees which interrupt is not the SVD's and why.

**The alternatives:** `cmsis-svd-data`'s copy, a third party's collection
of the same files; ST's own download, whose licence is ST's agreement and
whose URL serves whatever is current; taking the header's reading wherever
it disagrees, which would have widened two DMAMUX1 fields to DMAMUX2's;
and correcting no interrupt, which leaves a handler for the RAMECC
interrupt refused at its own slot.

**Pinned by** `devices/policies/stm32h753.json` and `devices/test.py`'s
`Stm32h753Oracles`, which compares every selected register and field's
address and layout with ST's header, the reset values and access policies
with literals reviewed from RM0433 Rev 9, each citing its section and page,
and the interrupts with the header's IRQ numbers and the manual's table;
and the `devices` suite's `a correction is recorded`, which holds an
interrupt correction's line and table.

### D561 — A consumer's device accesses are read from its linked image

**The tour said** nothing. No emulator models the STM32H753, and a board
run is R12's, not the importer's, yet the generated modules must be shown to
make the accesses their names promise.

**Chosen:** `devices/consumers/stm32h753` configures the UART transmit with
whole images computed in the program, and `devices/thumb.py` reads the
linked image: from its reset vector it evaluates the ARMv6-M instructions
the backend emits over memory that is the image's own bytes, and records
each store to a device window, with its address, width and value, until the
first WFI. The check compares that list, in order, with one reviewed from
RM0433's memory map and register descriptions, and requires that nothing
enables or maintains the M7's caches. The evaluation models no peripheral,
exception or clock: it reads the image, it does not run a chip.

**The alternatives:** QEMU's core with a recording model at the device's
addresses, which the reference profile's map allows and the STM32H753's,
from 0x0800_0000, does not; disassembling the image and matching patterns,
which a change of instruction selection breaks; and checking the IR, which
is not what is linked.

**Pinned by** `devices/test.py`'s `the consumer's linked accesses` and the
offline `the evaluator reads stores and their widths`, until D621 retired
the evaluation.

**Retired by D621:** the STM32H753's description has a float unit (D615),
so its consumer is hard-float Armv7E-M code, which an ARMv6-M evaluator
does not read, and a board now runs it. The board run's oracle checks the
consumer's device accesses in their place. What stays checked statically,
in `devices/test.py`'s `the consumer links cacheless`, is that the consumer
links where its description places it and that its image holds no literal
reaching SCB's CCR or the cache maintenance operations, which is how
nothing enables or maintains the M7's caches stays checked in the gate.
`devices/thumb.py` remains for RP2040's second stage (D588).

### D562 — The STM32H753's description is cacheless and keeps DMA out of the TCMs

**The tour said** nothing; the R12 phase admits a cached profile only with
its maintenance provider.

**Chosen:** `devices/descriptions/stm32h753/memory.ldn` describes 2 MiB of
flash from 0x0800_0000, the 64 KiB ITCM at 0, the 128 KiB DTCM at
0x2000_0000, 512 KiB of AXI SRAM at 0x2400_0000, SRAM1, SRAM2 and SRAM3 at
0x3000_0000, 0x3002_0000 and 0x3004_0000, and SRAM4's 64 KiB at
0x3800_0000, each checked against the base addresses of ST's header. The
boot kind is `vector-table`, the plain table at 0x0800_0000. The profile is
cacheless: compiler-owned startup leaves the M7's caches disabled, as reset
leaves them. DMA1 and DMA2 reach neither TCM, so initialized data, BSS and
the stack, where prototype 1's buffers are, are placed in the AXI SRAM,
which both streams reach; the DTCM is described and holds only what a
program places there by name. This profile stays the board's cacheless one,
its bytes and checks unchanged, beside the cached profile admitted with its
provider, `devices/descriptions/stm32h753_cached`, which a program selects
by importing it instead (D974).

**The alternatives:** the stack in DTCM, which is faster and puts any
buffer a routine passes to DMA where DMA cannot reach it; enabling the
caches here, which needed the maintenance provider the phase required
first, and which D974 does in a description of its own so that this one
and every program built for it are unchanged; and placing data in SRAM1,
which reaches no further and is smaller.

**Pinned by** `devices/test.py`'s `the hand-written memory against the
header`, which holds each region to the header and every placement DMA may
touch out of the TCMs, and the cache check of `the consumer links
cacheless` (D621); and `environments/cortex-m/descriptions.py`, which selects the
STM32H753 by importing its description at `--level=armv7e-m` and compares
its linked regions, vector table at 0x0800_0000 of 166 words, reserved
slots, USART3's handler at slot 55, a datum placed in the DTCM and its
plain-table boot with `descriptions.json`, recorded from ST's header. Its
capacity verdicts are those of `backend_corpus.py`'s `profiles`, measured
from each limited image's sizes and frames, as RP2040's are, because the
corpus links with the reference's probe map.

### D700 — A RISC-V description's core and identity are its policy's

**The tour said** nothing; D542 took the core from the SVD's `cpu/name`,
of which six Cortex-M spellings are read, and the identity from its
`device/name` in lowercase. Espressif's SVDs name their cpu `RV32IMC` and
`RV32IMAC`, which say nothing of the interrupt model a description's
slots follow, and name the device with a hyphen, `ESP32-C3`, which D556's
vendor names refused. RP2350's SVD says `CM33`, and its Hazard3 cores read
the same file.

**Chosen:** a policy may give `core`, one of `hazard3`, `esp-rv32imc` and
`esp-rv32imac-clic`, which `interrupts.ldn` then names whatever the SVD's
cpu says, and `identity`, the description's `compiler.device`, in D542's
form, where the SVD's name is not the one wanted; an SVD whose cpu is none
of the six Cortex-M names and a policy that names no core is L0528, saying
the policy names it. A policy's `device` may hold hyphens, as the SVD's
does; such a policy gives its `prefix` and `description`, which module
paths hold. Amends D542's step 5 and D556. `sifive-e31`, the fourth named RISC-V
core, has no SVD to learn and no policy names it.

**The alternatives:** reading `RV32IMC` as `esp-rv32imc`, which turns an
ISA string into an interrupt controller and would read every vendor's
RV32IMC the same; a second SVD for Hazard3, which nobody publishes; and
the identity `rp2350` for both of RP2350's descriptions, which two records
of `descriptions.json` cannot share.

**Pinned by** the `devices` suite's `a policy names the core` and `every
refusal is named`, `devices/policies/esp32c3.json`, `esp32c5.json` and
`rp2350_hazard3.json`, and `devices/test.py`'s `D542Form`.

### D701 — An interrupt matrix's sources are a module, not slots

**The tour said** nothing; D542's `compiler.interrupt(name, irq)` is an
external interrupt at slot 16 + irq, which is what an NVIC and Hazard3's
Xh3irq take. On the ESP32-C3 and ESP32-C5 the SVD's `<interrupt>` values
are the interrupt matrix's sources: each names a mapping register, which
routes the source to a CPU interrupt line, and only the lines are slots
(the C3's lines 1 to 31, the C5's CLIC identities 16 to 47, as their
cores' interrupt models say).

**Chosen:** on `esp-rv32imc` and `esp-rv32imac-clic`, `interrupts.ldn`
keeps D542's lines 1 to 4, its corrections' lines among them, adds after
them `-- Its interrupts are interrupt-matrix sources, not slots:
PREFIX/sources.`, and holds `compiler.device`, `compiler.core` and
`compiler.vectors(N)`, N the core's slots, 32 for a vectored mtvec's
mcause codes and 48 for the C5's CLIC, and no `compiler.interrupt`. The
sources, as the policy's corrections leave them, are generated as the
module `PREFIX/sources`, beside the register modules and in their
manifest: the policy's notice, two lines saying what a source is, the
corrections' lines, and `public NAME: u32 = N` for each, NAME the
interrupt's name in lowercase, ordered as D542 orders interrupts. A
program routes UART0 by writing a line into the register at
`interrupt_core0` offset four times `sources.uart0`. On every other core
D542's form is unchanged. Amends D542's steps 5 and 6.

**The alternatives:** listing the sources as `compiler.interrupt` at
16 + n, which gives slots the core does not have; dropping the sources,
which leaves a program to copy numbers out of a header; and generating
them into the description, whose directives are the compiler's and not a
program's names.

**Pinned by** the `devices` suite's `a policy names the core`, which holds
both texts, `devices/test.py`'s `D542Form`, which renders both from the
SVD apart from refine, and the oracles' `test_sources_against_the_header`.

### D702 — The ESP32-C3 and ESP32-C5 are learnt from their SVDs, ESP-IDF and their manuals

**The tour said** nothing; prototype 1's board application is to run on
the ESP32-C3 and ESP32-C5.

**Chosen:** the C3 is learnt from `espressif/svd` at
`be20aa12560889d6125d144cdb48cf615ac17628`, Espressif's repository of
SVDs and its newest commit, and the C5 from `esp-rs/esp-pacs` at
`a96d437ebad40b00854aa3e78011ad7732713a4d`, `esp32c5/svd/esp32c5.base.svd`,
since Espressif's repository has no C5. esp-pacs is Espressif's own Rust
team's, whose commits correct the base file in place, so it is the
vendor's copy and not D560's declined third-party collection; its policy
says `modified from it`. ESP-IDF v6.1, commit
`fff9895c82d744c7237be8847347bdd1b07c6643`, is each chip's oracle: its
`reg_base.h`, `soc.h`, the selected peripherals' `*_reg.h`, `interrupts.h`
and the C5's `clic_reg.h`. Where the SVD and the headers disagree, each
chip's Technical Reference Manual decides, the C3's v1.4 and the C5's
v1.1, pinned by hash and supplied by hand since their URLs serve the
current version, and the policy carries its correction with section and
page. Where both agree, the SVD stands even where the manual reserves a
bit. The C3's corrections: its one I2S's clock and reset bits are 21, not
4, and the I2S1 bits the SVD puts at 21 are omitted (16.5, Registers 16.3
and 16.5); and each selected pin's MCU_DRV, bits 6:5, is added (Register
5.21). The C5's: the interrupt matrix's mapping registers from MSPI's on
are eight bytes higher than the SVD puts them, UART0's at 0x0BC and
SYSTIMER_TARGET0's at 0x0F4 (11.6, p. 480; D704); each mapping register's
PASS_IN_SEC, bit 8, is added (11.7, p. 485); the timer groups' WDT_USE_XTAL
is omitted (Register 15.10); thirteen sources the SVD omits and the manual
and the header number alike are added, and BUS_MONITOR at 27, which the
header calls ASSIST_DEBUG (Table 11.5-1); and the CLIC is added (D705).
Where the manual agrees with the SVD the check names the header's
disagreement: the C3's RTC and super watchdog keys reset to zero, and the
C5's pin hysteresis bits exist. The selections are what the boards' port
touches: UART0, its pins and an indicator, the clock and reset gates of
UART0 and the system timer, UART0's and the system timer's routing, the
C3's line enables, types, priorities 1 and 2 and threshold, the C5's CLIC
configuration and identities 17 and 18, the system timer for a
millisecond wakeup, every watchdog a flash boot leaves running, and the
last reset's cause. Generated modules carry Apache-2.0's notice, in the
tree as `devices/notices/LICENSE-Apache-2.0.espressif`.

**The alternatives:** a third party's C5 SVD; esp-pacs's patched SVD,
which its build generates and nobody publishes at a fixed URL; taking the
headers' reading wherever it disagrees, which would have given the C5's
UART0 the SVD's wrong address and none of the manual's reservations; and
selecting every register of each peripheral, which the board does not
touch and no reviewer reads.

**Pinned by** `devices/test.py`'s `Esp32c3Oracles` and `Esp32c5Oracles`,
which compare every selected register's address and every field's place,
width, reset and access with the headers, the sources with
`interrupts.h`, and the reviewed literals with the manuals.

### D703 — An element of a register array is a register

**The tour said** nothing; D557 refused `dim` arrays, which neither
earlier device needed. Espressif's SVDs give the IO MUX's pins and the
GPIO matrix's selections as `NAME%s` arrays, which the boards' port
selects.

**Chosen:** a policy selects an element of a register array by its name,
the array's `%s` replaced by one of its indices: those `dimIndex` gives,
as a range `LOW-HIGH` or a list `A,B,C`, or 0 to dim - 1 without one. It
is generated as a register of its own at the array's offset plus its
position times `dimIncrement`, and the correspondence records it as a
`dim_element` with the array's name and the index. A `dimIndex` whose
count is not `dim` is L0529; an index the array lacks, L0530, saying how
an element is named; an array whose name has no `%s` or is written
`[%s]`, an element that is an alternate, and arrays of fields, clusters or
peripherals stay L0528. Amends D557.

**The alternatives:** expanding every element of a selected array, which
generates sixty registers to touch three; and selecting the array by its
`%s` name, which no module can spell.

**Pinned by** the `devices` suite's `an array element is a register`, and
the C3's and C5's IO MUX pins and GPIO selections.

### D704 — A reviewed correction may move a register

**The tour said** nothing; D556's corrections move fields, add or remove
interrupts and correct resets. The C5's SVD omits two mapping registers
and puts each one after them eight bytes low, UART0's among them.

**Chosen:** `register_corrections` gives a selected register's `offset`,
a multiple of four, and the `source` it was read from; the register is
generated there and the correspondence records the SVD's offset beside
the source. An offset the SVD already gives, an unaligned one and one of
an unselected register are each L0526.

**The alternatives:** correcting the SVD's file, which D559 pins by hash;
and a field or interrupt correction, which cannot move a register.

**Pinned by** the `devices` suite's `a policy corrects and adds
registers` and `every refusal is named`, and `Esp32c5Oracles`.

### D705 — A policy may add a peripheral the SVD lacks

**The tour said** nothing. The C5's CLIC, whose per-interrupt words enable,
prioritize and trigger its lines, is in no SVD: ESP-IDF's `clic_reg.h`
and the manual's 2.8.2 describe it.

**Chosen:** `peripheral_additions` gives a peripheral by name, its `base`,
its `source`, and its `registers`, each with its `offset`, `access`,
`reset` and `fields`, each field its `bits` and an optional `access`, and
a register array's `dim` and `increment`. refine writes each as the SVD's
own XML and reads it as if the SVD gave it last, so it is selected,
generated and refused as any of the SVD's, and the correspondence records
each of its registers with the addition's source. A fault in what the
policy adds is placed in the policy, not the SVD. Adding a peripheral the
SVD gives, a member outside those, and an array without both `dim` and
`increment` are L0526. The C5's policy adds `CLIC` at 0x2080_0000:
`MCLICCFG`, `CLICINFO`, and `CLICINT%s`, each interrupt's four bytes as
one word, which the manual says word accesses reach atomically (2.8.2.6,
p. 86), with CTL as its three implemented bits; `mintthresh` is a CSR and
not added.

**The alternatives:** leaving the CLIC to the board's own stores, which a
reviewer of the modules cannot see; a hand-written module beside the
generated ones, which nothing compares with the manual; and a
byte-register view, which D557's 32-bit registers do not take.

**Pinned by** the `devices` suite's `a policy corrects and adds
registers` and `every refusal is named`, and `Esp32c5Oracles`, which holds
the CLIC to `clic_reg.h` and the manual's 2.8.2.7.

### D706 — RP2350's Hazard3 cores have a description of their own

**The tour said** nothing; D635 learnt RP2350 for its M33s.

**Chosen:** `devices/policies/rp2350_hazard3.json` reads the same pinned
SVD as `rp2350.json` and selects the same registers but the M33's private
bus, `PPB`, whose NVIC and VTOR Hazard3 does not have; its core is
`hazard3` and its identity `rp2350-hazard3`. Its modules are under
`generated/rp2350_hazard3`, byte for byte the Arm side's, and its

interrupts, Hazard3's Xh3irq taking IRQ n at 16 + n as the NVIC does,
and the Pico 2's map of D636, `rp2350-image-block`. Hazard3's interrupt
control is its own CSRs, which no SVD describes.

**The alternatives:** one description for both kinds of core, which D543
cannot select by target; and reusing `rp2350`'s modules, which offers a
Hazard3 program the M33's NVIC.

D831 supersedes this decision in part: the Hazard3 policy writes its
